says: Ana founds a Team; Ben and Cho join by invitation, their own key binding, Ana's in-person verification of that key recorded on the Team, and consent. Ana grants an 'editors' group read, use and contribute, under her founder grant, with an approved member set of Ben and Cho whose evidence is their two current memberships. Each listed member acts within that grant: Ben contributes the Team's instructions collection and Cho its knowledge collection, each naming the editors grant, and both commit. Ana then configures a Google connection, sets policy version 2 whose admission rule names that connection and the hosted_domain claim example.com, and grants a 'readers' group read and use with its membership delegated to that connection by policy version 2. Dan signs in through that connection on his phone; his verified claim admits him as a member under the rule, and his read of the instructions collection, naming the readers grant and his claim, is answered with the collection Ben committed. What must come back is each commit and the read; what must not happen is a group member acting beyond read, use and contribute.
